failureMessage: waitForFunction takes an async predicate's promise as truthy and resolves at once, on every engine, so the test passes only while the page happens to be fast
fix: wait with until(page, fn, arg) from web-tests/page_until.mjs, which polls the page until the async predicate resolves truthy

failureMessage: a test that sleeps a fixed time guesses how long the page takes: too short on a slow runner, so it flakes, and wasted on every fast one
fix: wait for what the next check reads (waitForFunction, waitForSelector, until()), or move the page's clock with ctx.clock; where only real time will do, end the line `// waits on purpose: <reason>`

failureMessage: the page knows Google in two files only: web/drive.js, the remote store (Google Drive), and web/account.js, the identity provider (signing in with Google and the settings it keeps in the user's Drive); anywhere else, Google is a detail the rest of the page must not depend on
fix: move the Google-specific code or words into web/drive.js (the store, behind `remote`) or web/account.js (identity, behind the account it returns); a browser key or cache path named before this rule keeps its value as a constant alone on its line, `const NAME = "nor-drive-…";`
